comments.text:
THIS IS WHAT'S AVAILABLE TODAY!
(it seems that Microsoft decided somewhere in 2019 to remove this feature, making a lot of computers almost unusable)

1. In Intel Laptops - open intel graphics command center find the power option > on battery > Turn off adaptive brightness, go to "plugged in" and turn off adaptive brightness there as well.
2. AMD laptops - the issue that causes it is called Vari-Bright turn it off in the Radeon settings.
3. In Dell Laptops  - the setting is moved to the BIOS, restart the computer get into your BIOS > video > Dynamic backlight control > Disable that.

comments.text:
This is kind of late but Bite-size random, Please pin this so that people can see it! (Read below for help)




Option no.1 : 


Find your way to the control panel, Then press on power options. Then a setting should be selected (Like high performance or balanced or power saver) 
Depending on what setting you have selected, Press on the "Change plan settings button". Then a click on the blue text "Change advanced power settings".
There now should be a list with a bunch of pluses ( + ). Scroll down to display and click on the plus. There should be an "Enable adaptive brightness" Tab.
Click on it and turn that setting off. If there is no adaptive brightness tab. Go down to step 2.

Option no.2

If you don't have the adaptive brightness option, your monitor should have some sort of button that opens a menu or something.
I have the MSI MAG271CR Curved monitor, And it has a red button behind it on the bottom right of it. When I click it it opens up a menu with some tabs and different display options.
If you see an HDCR option, Turn it off or disable it. HDCR stands for 'high dynamic contrast range'. It essentially changes the contrast or brightness on your monitor depending on how bright your screen is. If you turn that off, Your monitor should stay at the desired or set contrast/brightness until enabled again.

comments.text: You CAN  fix the problem....On Windows 10...go to CHOOSE OR CUSTOMISE A POWER PLAN...click on CHANGE PLAN SETTINGS....click on CHANGE ADVANCED POWER SETTINGS....open DISPLAY BRIGHTNESS and set both to 0%.....open DIMMED DISPLAY BRIGHTNESS and set both options to 0%...((or just make sure the percentages are exactly the same).....open ENABLE ADAPTIVE BRIGHTNESS and make sure it  is off....MAKE SURE YOU SAVE YOUR  CHANGES!!  Problem sovled.Now I adjust my brightness manually on the little battery icon as I wish.
comments.author: @lynette599

comments.text:
One more thing, under "Power Options" click o "Change settings that are currently unavailable". On my personal laptop "Intel Graphics Settings" is added to the list. Default settings are "Maximum power saving", after i change this to "Maximum Performance" my screen is clear and bright again.  (the problem is not always the brightness, is the contrast of the LCD dynamically changing for saving power).
The brightness is the backlight power of the LCD (LED or CFL), and contrast is the voltage applied to every pixel in the LCD. Both have about the same result for the image. Check them both!
